questions.text: Clinical Validation Evidence: Proof it works: (1) Clinical trials or pilot studies; (2) Peer-reviewed publications; (3) Comparison with standard of care; (4) Validation on local population (not just Western data); (5) Sensitivity/Specificity metrics (for diagnostics); (6) Regulatory approval for clinical use.
questions.evidence_required: Clinical study reports, Publications, Regulatory approval letters
questions.africa_specific_notes: Western algorithms often fail on African diseases (e.g., Malaria vs Flu). Local validation is mandatory.

questions.text: Patient Safety Monitoring: Tracking harm: (1) Active pharmacovigilance (drug side effects); (2) Device vigilance (app errors); (3) Mortality/Morbidity tracking; (4) Readmission rates; (5) Missed diagnosis tracking.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Safety monitoring often weak. Digital platforms have a unique opportunity to track outcomes.

questions.text: Infection Prevention & Control (IPC): For physical touchpoints: (1) PPE availability for CHWs; (2) Sterilization protocols; (3) Waste disposal (sharps); (4) Hygiene training; (5) IPC audit results.
questions.evidence_required: IPC protocols, Audit reports, Supply logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: CHWs visiting homes can spread disease (e.g., Ebola/COVID) if IPC fails.

questions.text: Anti-Counterfeit Measures: Preventing fake drugs: (1) Sourcing from authorized distributors only; (2) Batch tracking/serialization; (3) Scratch-off verification codes (e.g., mPedigree, Sproxil); (4) Visual inspection protocols; (5) Supplier audits; (6) Quarantine procedures for suspect stock.
questions.evidence_required: Sourcing policy, Verification logs, Supplier audit reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: 10-30% of drugs in SSA are fake/substandard. Verification tech (SMS codes) is standard best practice.

questions.text: Cold Chain Integrity: Vaccine/Insulin safety: (1) Temperature monitoring (data loggers); (2) Alert system for excursions; (3) Backup power for fridges; (4) Transport validation; (5) Disposal of spoiled stock.
questions.evidence_required: Temp logs, Excursion reports, Disposal records
questions.africa_specific_notes: Power outages kill vaccines. Solar fridges and remote temp monitoring are essential.

questions.text: Bias Mitigation in AI: Fairness of algorithms: (1) Training data diversity (African representation); (2) Testing for skin tone bias (dermatology); (3) Testing for gender bias; (4) Performance parity across groups; (5) Bias audit reports.
questions.evidence_required: Dataset demographics, Bias audit reports, Performance metrics by group
questions.africa_specific_notes: Dermatology AI trained on white skin fails on black skin. This is a safety issue, not just fairness.

questions.text: Clinical Appropriateness: Relevance to local context: (1) Alignment with National Treatment Guidelines; (2) Local disease prevalence consideration (Malaria vs Flu); (3) Drug availability alignment (don't prescribe what's not there); (4) Cultural appropriateness.
questions.evidence_required: Protocol alignment docs, Local formulary checks
questions.africa_specific_notes: US/UK guidelines don't apply. Malaria is #1 killer. Guidelines must be local.

questions.text: Ethical Marketing & Claims: Truth in advertising: (1) No false cure claims; (2) Clear distinction between wellness and medical advice; (3) No predatory targeting of vulnerable; (4) Compliance with advertising regulations; (5) Influencer disclosure.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Herbal 'cures' for HIV/Diabetes common. Tech platforms must not amplify quackery.

questions.text: Conflict of Interest Management: Doctor incentives: (1) Disclosure of referral fees; (2) Disclosure of pharma ties; (3) Ban on prescribing for profit; (4) Transparency on ownership (if doctor owns pharmacy).
questions.africa_specific_notes: Doctors over-prescribing or referring to their own labs is a common issue.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Healthcare in SSA: Clinical safety is the bottom line. Counterfeit drug prevention is a unique SSA challenge. Algorithmic bias (skin tone) is a critical safety factor for AI.
